subject: chemistry
title: Planning your practical investigation and poster

lines.say: You design your own investigation on sustainable energy or materials, then make a poster.
A weak question is vague. Are biofuels good? You can't test that.
A strong question names the variables. Does alcohol chain length change energy per gram?
Then write a hypothesis. If, then, because.
If chain length increases, energy per gram increases, because there are more bonds to burn.
lines.write: more C–H, C–C bonds → more energy

lines.say: Here is a spirit burner heating a can of water.

draw.alt: Spirit burner under a can of water with a thermometer

lines.say: The independent variable is what you change. Here, the type of alcohol.

draw.alt: The burner, the thing you change, is highlighted

lines.say: The dependent variable is what you measure. The temperature rise of the water.

draw.alt: The thermometer, the thing you measure, is highlighted

lines.say: Controlled variables stay the same. Mass of water, the can, the distance to the flame.
Only one thing changes, so the test is valid.
Write steps another student could follow exactly, with sizes and repeats.
A risk assessment lists each hazard, its risk and your control.
Alcohols are flammable. Use small volumes and keep a fire blanket nearby.
Check the safety data sheet for every chemical.
Picture a dartboard. The bullseye is the true value.
Darts close together are precise. Darts on the bullseye are accurate.
This tight cluster misses the bullseye. Precise, but not accurate.

draw.alt: Left board: tight cluster off-centre. Right board: tight cluster on bullseye

lines.say: Trials of 20.1, 20.4, 20.0 and 20.3 agree closely. Precise.
But the data book says 29.6. So they are not accurate.
Random errors scatter readings above and below. They hurt precision.
Random? Repeat. More trials and an average reduce the effect.
Systematic errors shift every reading the same way. They hurt accuracy.
Heat lost from the can makes every result too low.

draw.alt: Heat escapes from the can into the air

lines.say: Systematic? Switch the method. Insulate the can and use a draught shield.
Spilling a sample is a mistake, not an error. Discard it and redo the trial.
Put units in column headings. Match decimal places to the equipment.
Use a line graph for continuous variables, a bar chart for categories.
Say your data support the hypothesis. Never say proven.
The poster is about 600 words. Title, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion, references.
Keep a logbook all the way through. It shows the work is yours.
I change it, it depends on it, I control the rest.
Hypothesis: if, then, because. No because, no full marks.
Repeatable means same person again. Reproducible means a different person.
Random? Repeat. Systematic? Switch the method.
